text:
Ava: Ran an nsys capture on staging for the KV/prefix cache regression around 14:02 PT. Hit ratio drops from ~86% -> 52% in the window, p99 spikes.
Diego: ugh. which model and batch pattern? any changes in kernel selector? :thinking_face:
Ava: locally on rwd-serve-v2, 8-GPU, model: rw-attn-13b-qlora. Workload: many short prefixes, heavy re-use on a small subset. Batching: adaptive heuristic recently changed to prefer larger micro-batches (>8) to boost throughput.
Sree: did you capture the kernel timeline? nvtx/trace?
Ava: attached nsys timeline snippet below (trimmed):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=kv-hitdrop-1402
Timeline: 14:02:03.120 - 14:02:05.800
GPU 0: matmul_fwd (40ms), attention_kv_lookup (6ms), attention_kernel (120ms), fallback_matmul (200ms)
Cache lookup latencies spike right before fallback_matmul calls.
```
Jordan: fallback_matmul is the fp32 fallback path that triggers when kernel selector can't find a quantized matmul for this seqlen/stride combo.
perf-bot: Regression alert: staging/rw-attn-13b-qlora p99 latency +12% vs baseline (yesterday). Cache hit ratio drop detected (86% -> 52%).
Diego: so kernel selection is picking the slower path mid-run. Any correlation with batch packing changes?
Ava: yes — when micro-batch consolidation happened, we started mixing sequences with very different seqlens. Kernel selector uses a (seqlen, stride, dtype) key; mixed batches increased selector misses and forced generic fallback.
Sree: interesting. Does prefix reuse heatmap show temporal locality? maybe evictions are racing with reuse.
Ava: I exported a KV access trace (timestamps + key ids) — reuse concentrated on ~3k keys, but eviction windows overlap because we aggressively prune after N unused tokens. Eviction TTL was reduced in last deploy from 300s->60s.
Jordan: that TTL change was to control memory growth. Looks like it regresses reuse-heavy workloads.
Diego: propose quick mitigation: increase TTL back to 300s and tweak batching heuristic to avoid mixing very short+long sequences in the same micro-batch. Also add a kernel-selector fallback cache for mixed-shape fingerprints.
Sree: from nsys flame: the expensive ops are attention_kernel (custom opt) and fallback_matmul. attention_kernel time increases when KV cache miss rate rises because KV loads become cache-miss bound and force extra mem copies.
Ava: perfetto screenshot shows frequent small memcpy calls right before attention_kernel spikes. Copy size ~12KB, many repeats.
Jordan: can we add warmup prefetch on cache miss path to overlap memcpy with compute? Even a small async prefetch might reduce stall.
Diego: longer-term: extend kernel selector to consider batch shape histograms and pick kernel variant that tolerates intra-batch shape variance. Short-term: TTL+batching tweak + revert adaptive consolidation.
perf-bot: Note: created an incident ticket #INC-4921 and linked profiler artifacts: s3://redwood-profiling/1799876500/.
Ava: I pushed a repro script to staging: `scripts/repro_kv_hitdrop.sh` — it mimics client pattern that hit the regression. Steps to repro in thread: 1) set TTL=60, 2) run load pattern A (prefix-heavy). Observed p99 regression within 3 mins.
Sree: I'll run the repro with syscall-level sampling + perfetto on my workstation to double-check host-side stalls. @Diego can you try reverting TTL in a canary? :thumbsup:
Diego: will do canary revert + hold adaptive consolidation for one hour. Updating rollout.
Jordan: also adding a small metric to the console: prefix_cache_evictions_per_min + kernel_selector_miss_rate to help catch this in future.
Ava: thanks — I also saved the nsys capture and exported kernel names/occurrence counts to CSV: `nvtx_kernel_counts.csv` in the artifact dir.
Diego: if rollback improves p99, we should ship a quick config rollback patch and follow up with selector improvements.
Sree: noted. I'll open a PR for conservative selector scoring and add unit tests for mixed-shape batches.
Ava: TL;DR: root cause = TTL reduction + batching consolidation -> kernel selector misses -> fallback runtime matmul + extra memcpy -> p99 spike. Short-term fix rolling now: TTL revert + batching lock. Longer-term: selector heuristics + prefetch.
Jordan: thanks all. Keep the thread updated with canary numbers.
perf-bot: Canary deployed: staging/canary-ttl-revert at 14:23. Canary p99 currently -4% vs baseline (good).
